However, Shanto noted that playing the world's best team leaves no room for errors, citing costly missed catches and numerous no-balls as decisive factors that ultimately cost them the match.

stories.title: Ten Killed in Ormara Collision Involving Passenger Coach and LPG Bowser
stories.summary:
At least 10 people, including a woman and a child, lost their lives and several others sustained burn injuries in a severe collision on Thursday. The accident occurred near Basol in Ormara along the Makran coastal highway when a Karachi-bound passenger coach collided with a liquefied petroleum gas bowser. Superintendent of Police for the Makran coastal highway police, Muhammad Aslam Bangulzai, confirmed the death toll.

According to police, the passenger vehicle was travelling from Turbat to Karachi when the impact took place. The collision immediately triggered a fire that engulfed both vehicles, trapping passengers inside before emergency responders could intervene. Rescue teams, coastal highway personnel, and local administration officials were dispatched to the site, and the injured victims were transferred to the Ormara Health Centre for medical treatment.

The accident caused major disruptions, leaving traffic on the Makran coastal highway suspended for several hours. Long queues of stranded vehicles formed near Basol and Ormara as a result of the blockage. This tragedy follows a series of fatal accidents on the same coastal highway in recent months, including an August crash that killed six family members, a March collision that claimed seven lives, and a January vehicle overturn that killed 10 people and injured over 30 others.

stories.title: COP31 Negotiators Release Revised Draft Deal Omitting Fossil Fuel References
stories.summary:
Climate negotiators at the COP31 summit in Antalya, Turkiye, published a slimmed-down draft deal on Thursday that completely removes any reference to ending the use of fossil fuels. The conference, facing an impending Friday deadline, is unfolding as global policymakers grapple with competing crises including war and soaring living costs, even as extreme weather events like droughts, heatwaves, and floods intensify worldwide. The revised text is significantly weaker than the initial draft released on Monday, stripping out targets for fossil fuel phaseouts, electrification, and a $120 billion adaptation finance goal for developing nations.

The removal of key provisions drew sharp criticism from observers and advocacy groups. Mohamed Adow, director of the think tank Power Shift Africa, warned that the current version risks rendering the summit a "ghost COP" with no tangible achievements. Despite the omissions, Thursday's draft retains an acknowledgment that global warming could surpass the critical 1.5 degrees Celsius threshold. It also calls for sustained, rapid greenhouse gas emissions cuts and encourages the deployment of carbon removal technologies, a provision critics argue may provide loopholes for the fossil fuel industry to continue polluting.

Australia, co-leading negotiations alongside Turkiye under a split presidency, maintained that the opening draft was always structured as a broad document intended to be narrowed. Historically, consensus among the nearly 200 participating nations frequently pushes proceedings past the official Friday closing schedule by more than 24 hours. Fundamental disagreements persist regarding financial responsibilities, mitigation strategies, and the required pace of climate action.

The updated document includes a non-binding call for global cooperation to elevate electricity's share of world energy consumption from roughly 23 percent to 35 percent by 2035. This goal, originally championed by host nation Turkiye and backed by approximately 75 countries, previously faced resistance from developing nations over funding concerns. Jasper Inventor, head of the Greenpeace COP31 delegation, argued that the electrification target lacks clarity on accelerating the fossil fuel transition and criticized carbon removal inclusions as a profound backward step for global climate efforts.

stories.title: Xi, Trump, and Putin Hold First Trilateral Summit at APEC in China
stories.summary:
The leaders of China, the United States, and Russia commenced their first trilateral meeting on Thursday on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China. Chinese President Xi Jinping, US President Donald Trump, and Russian President Vladimir Putin gathered at Kylin Villa for talks. While Beijing described the objective as safeguarding world peace, critics and analysts expressed concern that the high-level meeting is primarily symbolic and could signal an effort by major powers to carve out global spheres of influence.

The summit coincides with ongoing geopolitical conflicts, including Russia's military offensive in Ukraine nearing its fifth year, and a war involving Iran that has impacted global oil supplies and consumer prices. Before the three-way talks, Trump held his first meeting with Putin since August 2025, followed by a separate bilateral discussion with Xi, marking their third meeting of the year. The leaders' agendas varied across official accounts, with discussions touching on the Ukraine conflict, trade, artificial intelligence guidelines, and nuclear disarmament following the expiration of a bilateral US-Russia arms treaty in February.

The meeting drew sharp criticism from political opponents and analysts who warned that the optics would benefit the domestic standings of Xi and Putin while potentially undermining US interests. Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer accused Putin and Xi of manipulating the US president. Meanwhile, the summit featured notable diplomatic exchanges, including Xi greeting Trump with an airport reception involving an air-force flyover, a gesture reciprocating Trump's welcome in the US last September.

The APEC gathering also brought together other regional leaders, such as Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese. Despite underlying regional tensions, the leaders participated in traditional events, including the APEC family photo wearing special scarves. Xi opened the main summit proceedings by urging participating nations to lower barriers to trade and investment.

stories.title: Pakistan Navy Enhances Combat Capabilities Across All Operational Domains
stories.summary:
Chief of the Naval Staff Admiral Naveed Ashraf announced that the Pakistan Navy has significantly improved its combat readiness across all operational domains. Speaking at the graduation parade of the Pakistan Air Force Academy Asghar Khan in Risalpur, located in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Nowshera district, Admiral Ashraf emphasized that the navy is steadily modernizing its fleet.

Key advancements highlighted by the naval chief include the introduction of state-of-the-art warships, Hangor-class submarines, indigenously developed long-range weapons, unmanned systems, and the creation of the Pakistan Maritime Science & Technology Park. He noted that contemporary warfare is driven by rapid technological advancements and expanding into electronic warfare, cyber, space, cognitive fields, artificial intelligence, and autonomous systems.

Addressing the regional security climate, Admiral Ashraf pointed out that geopolitical dynamics have grown more complex due to tensions in the Middle East. He noted that the ongoing Operation Muhafizul Bahr, launched in March following the Middle East conflict, continues successfully. He also reflected on the May 2025 Pakistan-India conflict, known as Marka-i-Haq, stating that the armed forces proved invincible and capable of deterring aggression, with the navy successfully keeping the Indian Navy at bay.

Turkey’s air force chief, General Rafet Dalkiran, attended the parade as a guest. Admiral Ashraf praised the enduring friendship between Pakistan and Turkey, and reaffirmed that while Pakistan remains a peace-abiding nation dedicated to regional stability and diplomacy, its armed forces are fully prepared to defend the country against any threat.

stories.title: IEA Warns Middle East Crisis Poses Historic Threat to Energy Security
stories.summary:
The ongoing Middle East crisis, triggered in February by US and Israeli bombings of Iran, represents the largest threat to energy security in history, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA). In its flagship annual World Energy Outlook released in Paris, the agency warned that the disruption has far surpassed the scale of the oil shocks seen in the 1970s, leaving consumers to shoulder the burden of soaring prices and supply shortages.

Energy exports from the Gulf region have faced severe obstacles as Iran enforces a blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and targets nearby oil tankers. Despite American efforts to escort commercial vessels through the crucial channel—which previously handled roughly one-fifth of global oil shipments—supply chains remain heavily interrupted. IEA Executive Director Fatih Birol noted in the report that governments have tried to shield households by boosting supplies and utilizing alternative routes, but consumers continue to face higher costs and reduced availability.

Released concurrently with the COP31 climate talks in Turkey, the report incorporates scenarios evaluating how long-term disruption might alter global energy markets. In its standard middle scenario, the IEA projects that global oil demand will peak around 2030 before slowly declining, while gas demand is expected to grow until approximately 2035. However, additional scenarios factoring in a prolonged Middle East conflict indicate deep, lasting impacts.

Birol emphasized that as traditional buffers diminish, the global economy and energy sector are forced to absorb the shocks directly. He added that there is no foreseeable path for the global energy landscape to revert to its pre-crisis state.

stories.title: COMSATS University Offers Free Education for Industrial and Mine Workers' Children
stories.summary:
COMSATS University Islamabad (CUI) has announced 100 percent free education opportunities for eligible industrial and mine workers alongside their children under the Punjab Workers Welfare Fund (PWWF) Talent Scholarship Programme. The initiative applies to admissions for the Spring 2027 semester across multiple campuses, including Islamabad, Lahore, Abbottabad, Wah, Sahiwal, Vehari, and Attock.

Under this scholarship scheme, successful applicants receive fully funded education that covers their tuition fees, hostel accommodations, and daily transportation costs. The scholarship remains active for the normal duration of the chosen degree programme. However, students who are required to repeat a course or an entire semester must pay the standard dues outlined by university regulations.

To qualify for the PWWF scholarship, workers must meet specific criteria under the Industrial Relations Act of 2010, hold a valid Social Security Card, and possess a minimum of three years of work experience in a factory registered under the Factories Act of 1934 or a mine registered under the Mines Act of 1923. Additionally, employers must satisfy legal requirements under the Workers’ Welfare Fund Ordinance of 1971 or the Companies’ Profits (Workers’ Participation) Act of 1968. Children of deceased or disabled workers registered with EOBI or Social Security are also eligible if they meet family welfare conditions.

Prospective students must apply for the scholarship simultaneously while submitting their online admission applications to a single-degree programme. Applicants are required to deliver the necessary hard-copy documents directly to the admission office of their chosen campus before the respective deadline.

stories.title: Asif Zardari and Bilawal Bhutto to Discuss New Provinces and Constitutional Amendments
stories.summary:
Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari is scheduled to travel from Karachi to Islamabad to hold a high-level meeting with President Asif Ali Zardari. The discussions between the father and son will center on the country's current political landscape and internal party affairs.

According to sources, the agenda includes proposals regarding the creation of new administrative units and provinces, potential constitutional amendments, and the possibility of a national referendum. The talks come at a critical juncture as the PPP leadership weighs its official stance on various constitutional and political issues, alongside anticipated shifts in political alignments.

Another key item slated for discussion is the potential convening of a meeting of the PPP's Central Executive Committee (CEC). This proposed gathering would serve as a broader forum for party leaders to evaluate the prevailing political environment and formulate future strategic initiatives.

Political observers are closely monitoring the outcome of the meeting between President Zardari and Bilawal Bhutto Zardari. The decisions made during their discussions are expected to significantly influence the party's upcoming policy directions regarding regional governance and legislative reforms.

stories.title: inDrive Conducts Nationwide Safety Workshops and Training Across Pakistan
stories.summary:
Ride-hailing platform inDrive organizes regular nationwide safety workshops across Pakistan to cultivate road etiquette, personal accountability, and continuous learning among its drivers. The comprehensive curriculum goes beyond basic transit logistics to cover foundational road safety, including adherence to traffic laws, speed limits, pre-trip vehicle inspections, and defensive driving techniques suited for adverse weather conditions.

In addition to driving rules, the sessions focus on professional conduct, boundary management, and de-escalation strategies for handling aggressive, unpredictable, or intoxicated passengers. A dedicated passenger safety module instructs participants on maintaining professional etiquette, identifying safe boarding and drop-off zones, following agreed routes, and assisting elderly, disabled, or vulnerable commuters, alongside guidelines for handling roadside breakdowns, accidents, or security incidents.

The training also provides an in-depth walkthrough of inDrive's digital safety architecture. Drivers learn to use pre-ride tools displaying passenger ratings and exact destinations, privacy-protecting in-app calls and chats, and AI-powered moderation filters that ban non-compliant accounts. Active in-trip safeguards are covered, such as proactive trip monitoring for prolonged stops, encrypted in-app audio recording for conflict deterrence, emergency SOS integration for instant police or ambulance access, and designated trusted contacts for critical situations.

Furthermore, the program reviews financial security by highlighting inDrive's comprehensive accident and health insurance coverage in Pakistan, provided in partnership with Waada and renewed annually. This policy protects active rides by covering accidental death, total disability, immediate medical expenses, and hospital cash benefits. Through these behavioral workshops, digital guardrails, and financial protections, inDrive aims to empower drivers and protect commuters across the country.

stories.title: Chinese President Xi Calls for Complete Elimination of Nuclear Weapons
stories.summary:
Chinese President Xi Jinping has advocated for the comprehensive prohibition and complete destruction of nuclear weapons during a meeting with US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin. Speaking on Thursday, Xi emphasized that the ultimate objective is to build a world entirely free of nuclear arms.

According to China’s official Xinhua news agency, the Chinese leader stated that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought under any circumstances. He stressed that every possible effort must be directed toward preventing such a conflict from occurring.

The high-level meeting brought together the leaders of three major nuclear powers to discuss global security matters. Xi's remarks underscored Beijing's official stance on disarmament and the avoidance of atomic warfare.

The discussions highlight ongoing international dialogues regarding strategic stability and the reduction of nuclear arsenals. No further details regarding additional agreements from the gathering were provided.

stories.title: Nicholls and Phillips Lead New Zealand Fightback in First India Test
stories.summary:
New Zealand reached 243-5 at stumps on the opening day of the first Test against India in Wellington, recovering from a precarious 70-5 after lunch. Henry Nicholls scored an unbeaten 113, while Glenn Phillips finished the day not out on 94, rescuing the hosts with an unbroken 173-run partnership.

India captain Shubman Gill won the toss and elected to bowl on a testing Basin Reserve pitch with ample grass, prompting India's fast bowlers to utilize fuller deliveries aimed at the stumps. Fast bowler Jasprit Bumrah made a brilliant return to Test cricket after nearly a year away, taking 3-52 from 17 overs. Bumrah dismissed captain Tom Latham with the third ball of the innings, later adding Daryl Mitchell and Tom Blundell to his tally. New Zealand had slumped to 60-4 at lunch following early wickets by Bumrah, Anshul Kamboj, and Akash Deep.

Nicholls arrived at the crease early in the morning session and played with patience and control to secure his 12th Test hundred and his sixth at the Basin Reserve. He was dropped by Devdutt Padikkal on 102 after mistiming a pull shot off a delivery. Phillips joined Nicholls shortly after lunch and immediately accelerated the scoring with powerful drives and deft cut shots, putting pressure on the visiting bowlers.

Indian batting coach Sitanshu Kotak praised Bumrah's exceptional line, length, and movement on the pitch. Kotak noted that the less experienced bowlers in the squad could learn valuable lessons from Bumrah's adaptability to New Zealand conditions as the series continues.

stories.title: SECP Directs Companies to Transfer Unclaimed Dividends to Government Account
stories.summary:
The Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP) has ordered all listed companies to deposit dividends and profits that have remained unclaimed for three years into a designated federal government account. The directive was issued under a circular dated November 16, utilizing powers conferred by the SECP Act of 1997 and the relevant sections of the Companies Act.

Affected funds include unclaimed dividends on shares and modaraba certificates, as well as unclaimed profits on term finance certificates (TFCs) and sukuk. Companies are required to transfer these monies to Account No. G1120G, titled Companies Unclaimed Instruments and Dividend and Insurance Benefits and Investors Education Account, maintained under the Public Account of the Federation.

Before transferring the funds, companies must follow a mandatory compliance procedure. They are required to send a 90-day notice via registered post to the relevant shareholder. If no response is received, the company must publish an advertisement in newspapers inviting formal claims. If the amount remains unclaimed 90 days after the advertisement's publication, the company must deposit the funds into the government account.

Following the deposit, companies have seven days to submit the corresponding records to the SECP. Additionally, firms must publish lists of shareholders with unclaimed dividends and the respective amounts on their official websites, allowing investors to verify and claim their funds.

stories.title: Trump, Xi, and Putin Hold Historic Trilateral Meeting in China
stories.summary:
US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin convened for an unprecedented three-way meeting in Shenzhen, China, on the sidelines of an Asia-Pacific summit. Seated around a large round table inside a villa, the leaders of the world's largest nuclear powers opened discussions addressing regional conflicts, the war in Ukraine, and nuclear arms control.

While Putin noted shared interests in addressing conflicts like the one in Ukraine, and Trump pushed for nuclear arms control despite skepticism from analysts, Chinese state media highlighted Xi's focus on major powers living in harmony. Analysts noted that major agreements were unlikely due to deep disagreements concerning trade, Taiwan, Iran, and Ukraine. Patricia Kim from the Brookings Institution pointed out Beijing's reluctance to mediate the Ukraine conflict given the absence of European leaders.

Prior to the trilateral gathering, Trump held separate bilateral talks with both Xi and Putin, whom he referred to as friends. Trump's arrival in China featured elaborate welcoming ceremonies, contrasting with the more muted receptions of other officials, such as Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, whose presence came amid strained regional ties over territorial issues involving Taiwan.

The summit also served as a backdrop for broader geopolitical friction, including disputes over global trade protectionism, maritime energy flows through the Strait of Hormuz, and recent technology controls concerning advanced semiconductor chips. Craig Singleton of the Foundation for Defense of Democracies observed that while the meeting offered significant visual optics for all three leaders, substantive consensus on their complex policy differences remained out of reach.

stories.title: LPG Prices Drop Sharply Across Local Markets Following Increased Imports
stories.summary:
A surge in liquefied petroleum gas imports has led to a significant decline in local market prices, offering relief to consumers in Karachi. The per-kilogram rate for LPG fell by as much as 80 rupees, dropping from 530 rupees down to 450 rupees.

The price drop follows a continuous arrival of LPG cargo vessels at Port Bin Qasim. According to the Port Qasim Authority, six LPG carrier ships reached Pakistan between November 12 and 18, including the vessel Sea Shine, which recently docked carrying 21,866 tons of the commodity.

Prior to this influx, residents in Karachi faced severely inflated costs, with retailers selling the cooking and heating fuel far above the official government rate of 294 rupees per kilogram previously established by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority. These elevated charges had added substantial financial burdens to households even while general petroleum product prices saw reductions.

Separately, in academic updates, COMSATS University Islamabad announced it is providing fully funded education opportunities under the Punjab Workers Welfare Fund Talent Scholarship Programme for Spring 2027. Eligible industrial and mine workers alongside their children can access the tuition-free scheme across multiple campuses, including Islamabad, Lahore, Abbottabad, and Wah.

stories.title: Suspected Houthi Missile Strike Hits Riyadh Skyscraper Housing Wealth Fund HQ
stories.summary:
Riyadh's tallest skyscraper, serving as the headquarters for the Saudi Public Investment Fund (PIF), was struck on Thursday by a suspected incoming Houthi missile. The blast blew out windows across seven to eight floors of the PIF Tower and bent portions of its metal exterior. Entrances to the King Abdullah Financial District (KAFD) were immediately closed, people were evacuated, and emergency fire trucks and ambulances responded to the scene. There were no immediate reports of casualties. Three separate sources confirmed the building was hit by a Houthi missile, while the Saudi-led coalition stated it intercepted a projectile targeting Riyadh, resulting in fallen debris and material damage.

This incident marks the second time in under two weeks that a prominent landmark in the Saudi capital's financial district has sustained damage from a Houthi attack, following a November 8 strike on the headquarters of state oil giant Aramco. The PIF acknowledged receiving a media inquiry, while the Houthi movement did not immediately issue a formal statement. The renewed aerial assaults follow the breakdown of a 2022 ceasefire in July amid a broader regional conflict involving the United States, Israel, and Iran. Concurrently, the Houthi-run Saba news agency reported Saudi airstrikes in the Yemeni capital of Sanaa earlier on Thursday.

The escalating conflict poses a major challenge to Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman's economic diversification goals for the world's leading oil exporter. On Wednesday, the prince met in Riyadh with US Central Command chief Admiral Brad Cooper during his third publicized visit since hostilities resumed. Western officials indicate that Saudi military planning currently envisions a campaign lasting up to six months, with leadership seeking ground gains by allied forces before engaging in potential political negotiations. On the ground in Yemen, Houthi forces have recently captured extensive territory, including the entire Red Sea coast, the strategic Bab el-Mandeb Strait, and areas surrounding Taiz.

Wider regional hostilities have also intensified, featuring Iranian strikes against US allies Bahrain and Kuwait, alongside US airstrikes on Iran's Qeshm Island earlier in the week. Qatar-mediated negotiations between the primary belligerents have shown no signs of a breakthrough since fighting began in February. Saudi Arabia initially intervened in Yemen's civil war in 2015 at the head of an Arab coalition to reinstate the internationally recognized government after Houthi forces seized Sanaa.

stories.title: Fiji and Tonga Declare States of Emergency Amid Severe Drought
stories.summary:
Severe droughts driven by the El Nino weather pattern have escalated to crisis levels across parts of the South Pacific, prompting emergency declarations in both Fiji and Tonga. The El Nino phenomenon, which warms surface temperatures in the Pacific Ocean and disrupts normal precipitation cycles, is anticipated by experts to rank among the most powerful on record.

In Fiji, Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka announced a nationwide disaster declaration after water sources dropped to critical levels and prolonged dry conditions began heavily impacting daily life, farmers, crops, and livestock. The emergency measures grant authorities the power to ration water, mandate evacuations, and redirect public funds toward disaster relief efforts, with water-supplying trucks dispatched to assist parched rural communities.

Similarly, Tonga implemented a 27-day state of emergency to combat mounting water shortages and agricultural strain. Acting Prime Minister Viliami Latu emphasized that the emergency directive will streamline coordination for emergency services delivering critical assistance to protect public health and resources.

Additionally, academic institutions announced scholarship updates during the same period. COMSATS University Islamabad announced full education funding for eligible industrial and mine workers and their children through the Punjab Workers Welfare Fund Talent Scholarship Programme for Spring 2027 admissions, applicable at its Islamabad, Lahore, Abbottabad, and Wah campuses.

stories.title: Punjab Government Awards Smartphones to Winners of Kisan Card Draw
stories.summary:
The Punjab government, led by Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz Sharif, has revealed the successful farmers chosen in the second lucky draw of Phase IV of the Kisan Card initiative. Ten farmers were selected to receive smartphones as part of the provincial administration's efforts to modernize the agricultural sector and provide technological support to the farming community.

Promoted under the official slogan "Maryam Nawaz’s Dream – A Punjab That Grows Gold," the initiative aims to enhance productivity and facilitate greater integration of modern practices among local farmers. The names and identification details of the ten fortunate winners have been publicly released through official notices.

The Kisan Card program functions as a core provincial effort to deliver financial and agricultural assistance. Farmers seeking further guidance or support regarding these agricultural assistance programs can contact the Punjab Agriculture Department helpline from 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM daily.

In separate institutional announcements, COMSATS University Islamabad disclosed that it is providing fully funded educational opportunities under the Punjab Workers Welfare Fund Talent Scholarship Programme for Spring 2027 admissions. Eligible industrial and mine workers, as well as their dependents, can apply for the 100 percent fee waiver across university campuses located in Islamabad, Lahore, Abbottabad, and Wah.

stories.title: PM Sharif and President Zardari Agree to Resolve Issues Through Dialogue
stories.summary:
Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and President Asif Ali Zardari held a meeting at Aiwan-e-Sadr in Islamabad on Thursday, agreeing to resolve all outstanding national issues through mutual consultation and dialogue. The high-level discussion followed political turbulence sparked by critical remarks from Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari regarding governance and potential administrative restructuring, which drew sharp rebukes from federal government representatives. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, who has been a central figure in the recent political dispute, also participated in the session. Alongside domestic political matters, the leaders reviewed regional developments with a specific focus on the Middle East crisis and reaffirmed that previous constitutional amendments were achieved collaboratively among coalition partners.

State officials welcomed the presidential meeting as a mature and democratic approach to addressing political friction. State Minister for Interior Talal Chaudhry emphasized that political disagreements should be settled through consensus negotiations, describing Bilawal as an emotional leader while praising President Zardari's historical preference for dialogue. However, Chaudhry also questioned why the PPP chairman demanded restraint from government officials while launching sharp public criticisms himself. He dismissed suggestions of non-political conspiracies, reiterating that major decisions, particularly those involving a primary coalition partner like the PPP, will not be made unilaterally.

The political storm intensified following Bilawal's speech at the Karachi Press Club, where he warned of imminent civil unrest if Sindh's geographical boundaries were altered and alleged that the 27th Constitutional Amendment was coerced onto PPP lawmakers. Bilawal's remarks provoked strong reactions from other political figures, including Adviser to the Prime Minister on Political Affairs Rana Sanaullah and Defence Minister Khawaja Asif, who questioned the PPP's moral standing given its lengthy political tenure in Sindh. The underlying debate regarding the creation of new administrative units was originally initiated on July 31, when Interior Minister Naqvi argued at the Pakistan Economic Summit 2026 that the existing governance model had collapsed and required systemic overhauls.

Proposals to carve new provinces or administrative zones have drawn polarized reactions across Pakistan. While the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) has repeatedly advocated for administrative divisions within Sindh, the Sindh Assembly passed a unanimous resolution on September 4 rejecting any partition and vowing to protect the province's territorial unity. Government representatives have maintained that discussions regarding administrative performance and governance reforms should be debated democratically and extended nationwide rather than isolating a single province.

stories.title: Islam Projected to Surpass Christianity as World's Largest Religion by 2035
stories.summary:
According to a study published on Wednesday by the Washington-based Pew Research Centre, Islam is expected to overtake Christianity as the largest religion globally by the middle of the next decade. While Christianity has held this position for centuries, researchers project that the global Muslim population will reach 2.57 billion by 2035, narrowly exceeding the anticipated Christian population of 2.52 billion for that year. If current patterns continue, Muslims are expected to outnumber Christians 3.6 billion to 3 billion by the year 2070.

By 2070, Islam is forecast to make up 37 percent of the global population, up from 26 percent in 2020, while Christianity is projected to remain steady at approximately 29 percent. Furthermore, Pakistan's Muslim population is anticipated to double from 227 million in 2020 to 461 million by 2070, enabling the country to transition from the second-largest Muslim population to the largest in the world.

The demographic shift is largely attributed to higher fertility rates among Muslim women, who averaged 3.1 children each between 2020 and 2025, compared to 2.5 children per Christian woman. During the same period, all other religious categories combined averaged 1.6 children per woman, falling below the 2.1 threshold required for a generation to replace itself. Natural population growth remains the primary driver behind these demographic changes.

Religious switching will also influence the numbers, though both major faiths are expected to experience a net loss of adherents. Between 2020 and 2070, Islam is projected to lose 8 million adherents through switching, whereas Christianity is expected to lose 105 million. Globally, the overall human population is projected to grow by 29 percent between 2020 and 2070, with Islam and Christianity being the only two religious groups forecast to meet or exceed that expansion rate.

stories.title: European Stocks Rise as Tech Gains Offset Three Days of Declines
stories.summary:
European equities recovered on Thursday, breaking a three-day losing streak driven by a slump in mining stocks that had pulled the market to a three-week low on Wednesday. The pan-European STOXX 600 index advanced 0.3 percent to reach 645.85 points by 0822 GMT. Market sentiment was lifted by strong performance in the technology sector and developments surrounding a major corporate takeover in Germany.

Technology shares led the sectoral gains across Europe, boosted by investor optimism surrounding artificial intelligence and chip manufacturing. Chip-related companies including ASML, STMicroelectronics, and Infineon posted gains between 3 percent and 5.5 percent. This positive momentum followed an announcement by AI lab Anthropic, which raised $81.3 billion in the largest stock-market debut in history after upsizing its offering. The massive debut valued the Claude chatbot maker at $1.5 trillion ahead of its Nasdaq debut, easing broader investor concerns regarding tech fundraising and the AI market.

In corporate news, Germany and UniCredit reached an agreement regarding the key sticking points in the planned takeover of Commerzbank. Following the accord, Commerzbank shares rose 1.4 percent, while UniCredit shares added 1.8 percent. Additional stock movements included France's Soitec, which surged 12.7 percent after beating market expectations with its fiscal 2027 forecast. Conversely, Swiss drugmaker Novartis saw its shares drop 2.5 percent after setting its mid-term sales growth targets at the lower end of its previous projections.

stories.title: Robert Pattinson Named as New James Bond After Audition Process
stories.summary:
Actor Robert Pattinson has been announced as the new actor to play James Bond, succeeding Daniel Craig following several months of speculation. Reports indicate that Pattinson received $1 million simply for his audition, and his three-year contract could ultimately yield close to $100 million, with financial estimates placing his potential earnings between $76 million and $98 million.

Initially joining the shortlist as a late addition alongside Jack Lowden, Callum Turner, and Josh O’Connor, Pattinson was backed by Amazon MGM Studios despite the franchise's historical preference for lesser-known talent. Amazon founder Jeff Bezos confirmed his heavy involvement in the selection process, noting that while the team was initially biased against Pattinson due to his existing fame, his screen test with costumes and franchise scenes made his suitability obvious.

Pattinson's successful screen test also reportedly impressed Lauren Sanchez, the wife of Jeff Bezos. Director Denis Villeneuve informed the 40-year-old actor that he had secured the part on Sunday, just one day prior to the official Monday announcement. The casting marks a major new chapter for the long-running spy film series.

The selection process involved five finalists and rigorous screen tests, ultimately resulting in Pattinson stepping into the iconic role. This transition follows the tenure of previous 007 actor Daniel Craig, bringing high anticipation and substantial financial backing from Amazon MGM Studios to the upcoming films.

stories.title: US, Russia, and China Issue Historic Joint Stability Declaration
stories.summary:
Leaders from the United States, Russia, and China have issued a joint declaration pledging to preserve strategic stability, enhance international security, and improve dialogue regarding nuclear risk reduction and non-proliferation. The agreement was released following a trilateral summit in Shenzhen, China, attended by US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin, and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

The four-point declaration addresses several key areas of potential cooperation among the three permanent members of the United Nations Security Council. Regarding global governance, the leaders committed to reforming the United Nations to better address international challenges while upholding its core mission of maintaining peace. On energy, the nations stated an intention to boost the production and supply of refined petroleum products to ensure stable global energy flows.

Additionally, the declaration emphasizes the importance of state consent and the immunities of state officials, asserting that bodies like the International Criminal Court must not abuse their jurisdiction. On nuclear security, the leaders reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought, agreeing to cooperate on preventing nuclear proliferation.

Chinese President Xi Jinping described the summit as positive, constructive, and fruitful, emphasizing that major nations must take legitimate security concerns seriously and prioritize dialogue over conflict. Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump also expressed appreciation for China hosting the unprecedented diplomatic meeting.

stories.title: MQM-P Leader Questions Threats of Violence Over New Provinces in Sindh
stories.summary:
Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan (MQM-P) convener Dr Khalid Maqbool Siddiqui on Thursday criticized warnings of bloodshed regarding the potential creation of new provinces, questioning why such threats were directed exclusively at Karachi and Hyderabad. Speaking at a press conference in Karachi, Siddiqui noted that demands for new administrative regions have emerged across various parts of Pakistan, including Punjab and Hazara, without drawing warnings of violence in cities like Multan, Chakwal, or Abbottabad.

Siddiqui accused the Pakistan Peoples Party (PPP) of engaging in linguistic politics and urged party leader Bilawal Bhutto Zardari to adopt a national perspective rather than a narrow outlook. He maintained that MQM-P's push for new provinces stems entirely from population growth and administrative necessity rather than linguistic divisions, noting that the PPP previously established districts such as Malir and Keamari on administrative and political grounds. He further challenged authorities and the courts to take notice of statements threatening violence.

Addressing local security and upcoming political events, Siddiqui stated that the party would not be intimidated by threats, emphasizing that urban Sindh residents know how to defend themselves. Regarding MQM-P's planned November 29 rally, he mentioned that law enforcement agencies had requested a schedule review due to prevailing security concerns, and the party intends to announce a new date following internal consultations.

In a separate development announced on the same day, COMSATS University Islamabad revealed plans to offer fully funded education under the Punjab Workers Welfare Fund Talent Scholarship Programme for Spring 2027 admissions. The initiative targets eligible industrial and mine workers alongside their children, extending across campuses in Islamabad, Lahore, Abbottabad, and Wah.

stories.title: Pakistan Foreign Ministry Informs LHC Regarding Detained PTI Citizens in UAE
stories.summary:
The Ministry of Foreign Affairs informed the Lahore High Court that two Pakistani citizens linked with the PTI are being held in Abu Dhabi’s Al-Wathba Jail over state security cases. The ministry stated that diplomatic norms prevent Pakistan’s mission from interfering in internal matters of the host country, addressing the contempt of court petitions filed by the families.

According to the official reports submitted, Syed Salman Raza Zaidi has been convicted in a state security case and is currently classified as an undertrial prisoner, while Muhammad Junaid Jahangir was detained on September 24, 2024, in connection with a similar case. Justice Tariq Mahmood Bajwa disposed of the contempt petitions following the submissions, although legal counsel Barrister Abuzar Salman Niazi criticized the ministry for lacking substantive information and failing to provide charge sheets to the families.

The ministry detailed that the Pakistan mission in Abu Dhabi coordinated prison visits for both detainees after requests were submitted in June 2025. Embassy officials met with Zaidi in July 2025 and reported him to be in generally good health. The reports also noted that initial search and investigation requests were sent to UAE authorities in November 2025 and February 2026, though responses are still awaited.

Earlier hearings highlighted the Lahore High Court's dissatisfaction with previous ministry reports, leading to directives for the foreign secretary to process representations concerning the detainees. Counsel for the families announced intentions to file fresh petitions before the court to seek further legal clarity and disclosure regarding the detentions.

stories.title: Balochistan Approves Largest Public-Private Partnership for Sui Fertiliser Complex
stories.summary:
The Balochistan government has approved an $895 million urea fertiliser complex in Sui, located in the Dera Bugti district, through a public-private partnership framework. Officials confirmed this initiative marks the largest public-private partnership project in the history of the province, aimed at boosting local industrial growth and agricultural productivity.

The approval was granted during the 10th Public-Private Partnership Board meeting, which was chaired by Chief Minister Mir Sarfraz Bugti. The complex will be constructed on a 496-acre plot and will utilize indigenous low-BTU natural gas, consuming 100 million standard cubic feet per day to produce an estimated annual output of 580,800 metric tons of urea.

Project projections indicate a net present value of $301 million, an equity internal rate of return of 25.1 percent, and a payback period of nine years. Construction and operational timelines anticipate that full production at the facility will officially commence by April 2031.

Government representatives emphasized that the project will attract substantial private investment and generate vital economic opportunities within the region. The initiative is intended to strengthen domestic fertilizer supplies while driving sustainable economic development across Balochistan.

stories.title: Dua Lipa Prepares Fourth Album Ahead of Coachella Headline
stories.summary:
British singer Dua Lipa has traveled to Los Angeles for secret photoshoots as she prepares for the release of her fourth studio album, which is anticipated to drop in early 2027. Music insiders report that the record is nearly complete, shifting the primary focus to the promotional campaign and visual content for the upcoming launch.

The new musical era is scheduled to build toward Lipa's headline performance at the Coachella music festival in April 2027. Her record label has made the singer a major priority, investing heavily in the rollout of the project. This follows her 2024 studio album, Radical Optimism, and an extensive subsequent world tour that featured more than 80 stadium shows.

For the upcoming tracks, Lipa has reportedly collaborated with producer and songwriter Mark Ronson, with whom she previously worked on hit singles such as "Dance the Night" and "Electricity." Her personal life, including her marriage to actor Callum Turner, is expected to influence the lyrical direction of the new material.

Lipa has indicated an interest in exploring the quieter complexities of relationships and the experience of finding lasting love rather than heartbreak. The upcoming release represents the next major milestone in her career following her extensive touring and commercial success.

stories.title: Punjab Government Launches Online Portal for Women's Land Inheritance Claims
stories.summary:
The Punjab government has launched a digital platform allowing women to claim their lawful shares in family property online. The newly introduced facility utilizes the Revenue Case Management System portal to simplify the land division process for female citizens across the province.

Through this digital service, women can use their mobile phones to access the portal and begin procedures for securing their property rights. The initiative is designed to eliminate complicated bureaucratic procedures, reduce traditional paperwork, and minimize reliance on intermediaries during land distribution proceedings.

To complement this technological shift, provincial authorities have also established district-level committees tasked with addressing complaints about violations of women's inheritance rights. These committees hold the authority to recommend disciplinary action against government officials found guilty of negligence or misconduct.

These updates form part of wider efforts by the Punjab Land Records Authority to modernize local revenue administration. By integrating technology into land management, the administration seeks to enhance transparency and improve public access to ownership records.

stories.title: میکڈونلڈز کے خلاف سیکس سکینڈل: سابق ملازمہ نے سنگین الزامات عائد کر دیے
stories.summary: میکڈونلڈز کی ایک سابق ملازمہ ہوپ نے کمپنی پر سنگین الزامات عائد کرتے ہوئے کم عمر ملازمین کے ساتھ برتاؤ کا طریقہ تبدیل کرنے کا مطالبہ کیا ہے۔ 2023 میں ویسٹ مڈلینڈز کی برانچ میں کام کرنے والی ہوپ نے بتایا کہ وہاں کا ماحول انتہائی زہریلا اور جنسی نوعیت کا تھا۔ ان کا کہنا ہے کہ وہ اپنے سے عمر میں بڑے ساتھی ملازمین کو 16 اور 17 سالہ کارکنوں کو گھورتے ہوئے دیکھتی تھیں جو ان کے 18 برس کے ہونے کا انتظار کرتے تھے۔ ہوپ نے ایک منیجر پر بھی الزام لگایا کہ وہ گاہکوں کے جنسی اور توہین آمیز رویے کے دوران تحفظ دینے میں ناکام رہا اور اسے برداشت کرنے کا کہا۔ یہ تازہ پیش رفت اس وقت سامنے آئی ہے جب لندن سینٹرل ایمپلائمنٹ ٹربیونل کے جج گلینی نے میکڈونلڈز کی جانب سے 450 مقدمات خارج کرنے کی کوشش کو مسترد کر دیا ہے۔ یہ قانونی کارروائی قانونی فرم لی ڈے کے تحت کی جا رہی ہے اور امید ہے کہ ان مقدمات کی باضابطہ سماعت اپریل میں ہوگی۔ ہوپ نے واضح کیا کہ ان کا مقصد پیسے کمانا نہیں بلکہ نوجوانوں کی حفاظت کو یقینی بنانا اور میکڈونلڈز کے نظام کو بدلنا ہے۔ دوسری جانب میکڈونلڈز کے ترجمان نے کہا ہے کہ ریستورانوں میں محفوظ اور باوقار ماحول ان کی بنیادی ترجیح ہے اور وہ ہراسانی یا امتیازی سلوک کو کسی صورت برداشت نہیں کرتے۔

stories.title: Pew Research Center Projects Islam to Surpass Christianity by Mid-2030s
stories.summary:
Islam is projected to overtake Christianity as the world's largest religion by the middle of the next decade, driven by higher birth rates among Muslim populations. According to a study published by the Pew Research Center, the global Muslim population is forecast to reach 2.57 billion by 2035, narrowly exceeding the projected Christian population of 2.52 billion.

If current demographic trajectories continue, Muslims are expected to reach 3.6 billion compared to 3 billion Christians by 2070, making up 37 percent of the global population. Christianity is predicted to remain stable at around 29 percent. The primary driver behind this demographic shift is fertility rates, with Muslim women averaging 3.1 children compared to 2.5 children for Christian women between 2020 and 2025.

Religious switching will also influence future demographics, though both major faiths lose more adherents than they gain through conversion. Between 2020 and 2070, Islam is projected to lose approximately 8 million adherents through switching, while Christianity is expected to lose 105 million. Meanwhile, the overall global population is expected to grow by 29 percent over the same fifty-year period.

Geographic distributions of religious groups are likewise undergoing significant transitions. By 2070, Christianity will remain the largest religion in the United States but will lose its majority status, while the Democratic Republic of Congo is projected to surpass the US in Christian concentration. Additionally, the proportion of religiously unaffiliated individuals is expected to decrease globally, dropping from 24 percent in 2020 to 17 percent by 2070.

stories.title: Markazi Muslim League Serves Rs5 Billion Defamation Notice on Azma Bokhari
stories.summary:
The Markazi Muslim League has issued a legal notice demanding Rs5 billion in damages from Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari over statements labeling the party as a terrorist and banned organization. Khalid Masood Sindhu, president of the Markazi Muslim League, filed the notice, which demands a public apology, a retraction of the allegations, and the removal of related content from social media within seven days.

The contested remarks were allegedly published on Bokhari's personal account on X and subsequently broadcast by multiple media outlets. The legal notice asserts that the statements are false and defamatory, emphasizing that the Markazi Muslim League is a formally registered political party with the Election Commission of Pakistan that has engaged in political and welfare work since 2022.

In addition to the financial damages and public apology, the notice requires Bokhari to promise in writing that she will not repeat such remarks. It warns that failure to meet these conditions within the seven-day period will prompt the party to pursue legal action in court and potentially approach the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act.

Separately, the Punjab government rolled out a digital facility via the Revenue Case Management System online portal to simplify family land divisions, allowing women to claim their legal property rights using mobile phones.

stories.title: Trump, Xi, and Putin Set to Meet at APEC Summit in Shenzhen
stories.summary:
Leaders from the United States, China, and Russia are scheduled to gather for a high-profile three-way meeting during the annual Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, a technology hub in southern China. US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin are meeting against a backdrop of global conflicts, including ongoing wars in Ukraine and the Middle East. While advocates argue that direct dialogue is essential for addressing nuclear non-proliferation, artificial intelligence safety, and regional conflicts, analysts predict substantial practical breakthroughs will be scarce. Russia and China have not restrained North Korea's nuclear ambitions, with Moscow reportedly assisting Pyongyang in exchange for troops to fight in Ukraine. Furthermore, differing economic incentives complicate cooperation on conflicts involving Iran, while competitive dynamics limit potential agreements on artificial intelligence.

All three leaders arrive at the summit facing domestic vulnerabilities. Trump recently suffered a setback in US midterm elections where Republicans lost control of Congress and state governments. Putin continues to face setbacks in Ukraine, and Xi grapples with domestic economic difficulties and military leadership purges. Observers warn that an embattled Trump might attempt overly ambitious compromises, risking unfavorable concessions akin to the historical Yalta Conference. Ultimately, experts suggest that a basic diplomatic photo-op may be the most realistic and preferable outcome of the summit, preventing risky concessions while maintaining basic channels of communication among the world's major powers.

stories.title: Pakistan International Airlines Privatisation Expected to Yield Rs90 Billion in 2027
stories.summary:
The privatisation of Pakistan International Airlines has generated Rs80 billion in fresh equity alongside Rs10 billion for the government, with an additional Rs90 billion anticipated from the next phase in June 2027, according to Muhammad Ali, the prime minister’s adviser on privatisation. Speaking at the sixth Pakistan Prosperity Forum in Islamabad, Ali emphasized that privatisation aims to introduce modern expertise and capital rather than merely transfer shares.

State-owned enterprises recorded losses totaling Rs342.8 billion during the first six months of fiscal year 2026, while government financial support for these entities rose by 31 percent to a record Rs804 billion. Ali stressed that national resources should prioritize public welfare, education, and health instead of covering public sector losses, noting that the government's primary role is regulation and policymaking rather than running commercial enterprises.

Additional privatisation efforts include bringing a global investor into the market through the sale of First Women Bank, while due diligence is underway for power distribution companies IESCO, GEPCO, and FESCO. Furthermore, a public-private partnership is projected to attract $672 million in investment for the M-6 motorway.

Ali concluded that the true measure of privatisation success is the creation of economic value rather than the sheer volume of entities sold. He asserted that Pakistan's economic future relies on policy clarity, mutual cooperation, and consistent actions despite global uncertainties.

stories.title: Lionel Messi and Inter Miami Chase Back-to-Back MLS Cup Titles
stories.summary:
Lionel Messi and Inter Miami enter the Major League Soccer playoffs aiming to secure back-to-back MLS Cup championships for the first time in nearly fifteen years. Despite a regular season marked by coaching changes and poor home form, Messi secured a second consecutive Golden Boot with 26 goals and 17 assists, positioning himself for a potential third straight MLS MVP award.

Miami's roster also features veteran Uruguayan striker Luis Suarez, who scored 17 goals, and Brazilian midfielder Casemiro, supporting a squad that finished second in the Eastern Conference. To repeat as champions—a feat last achieved by the LA Galaxy in 2011 and 2012—Miami must navigate a postseason bracket that begins with a home match against the Columbus Crew.

Major challengers include Nashville SC, who set a single-season points record of 77 and captured the Supporters’ Shield under head coach B.J. Callaghan. Driven by Hany Mukhtar and Sam Surridge, Nashville aims to capture their first MLS Cup, though they must overcome historical superstition, as only two Supporters' Shield winners have claimed the title over the past fourteen seasons.

In the Western Conference, top-seeded Vancouver Whitecaps enter the postseason following a historic regular-season campaign under Jesper Sorensen, setting club records with 19 wins, 64 points, and 74 goals scored. Despite the midseason departure of American midfielder Sebastian Berhalter, the Whitecaps look to secure their first MLS Cup title after falling to Miami in last year's final.

stories.title: Bangladesh Strike and Protests Erupt Ahead of Hasina Return
stories.summary:
Parts of Bangladesh experienced shutdowns and nationwide protests called by former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina’s Awami League party. The demonstrations follow the government's rejection of Hasina's request for a new passport and identity card to facilitate her planned return in December. Police reported two ruling party members were killed in the surrounding violence, which has also involved dozens of crude bomb blasts and torched vehicles across 28 districts over the past ten days.

Amid the unrest, the ancestral home of former interim leader Muhammad Yunus in Chattogram was set ablaze late Wednesday after flammable substances were reportedly thrown into an unused ground-floor room. Family members residing on the upper floors remained safe. Additionally, at least 37 branches and offices of Grameen Bank, founded by Yunus, have been targeted in arson attacks since November 10. Security measures have intensified, with 97 platoons of the Bangladesh Border Guard deployed across seven districts.

Authorities have taken several legal and enforcement actions against political figures linked to the turmoil. On Thursday, police detained former education minister Nurul Islam Nahid at his Dhaka home regarding killings tied to the 2024 student-led uprising. That uprising led to Hasina fleeing to India in August 2024, followed by a local court sentencing her to death in absentia exactly one year prior to recent developments.

Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed accused exiled Awami League leaders of inciting supporters to destabilize the country and burn property, warning that perpetrators will face prosecution. The ongoing protests and security deployment highlight deep political polarization in Bangladesh as the country navigates the fallout from Hasina's ouster and her controversial return plans.

stories.title: APEC Leaders Meet in Shenzhen to Boost Regional Trade Openness
stories.summary:
The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting convened in Shenzhen, China, bringing together representatives from 21 member economies that collectively produce over 60 percent of global GDP. Chaired by Chinese President Xi Jinping, the forum focused on navigating rising protectionism, enhancing digital connectivity, and expanding investment opportunities amid an expected regional economic growth rate of 3.4 percent for 2026.

Discussions during Leaders' Week addressed various structural challenges, including regulatory hurdles, mismatched customs procedures, and rising energy costs that drive projected inflation to 3.2 percent. To counter these pressures, members explored initiatives such as China's proposed 2035 connectivity framework, aimed at streamlining supply chains, lowering transaction costs, and facilitating the movement of digital services and advanced manufacturing.

Business leaders and economic experts at the accompanying CEO Summit emphasized that trade is not a zero-sum game, highlighting potential collaborations in artificial intelligence, critical minerals, and agricultural market access. Figures such as economist Jeffrey Sachs and representatives from Chile, Indonesia, and Mexico underscored the necessity of cross-border technological exchange and talent development to maintain economic momentum.

Despite operating on a consensus model without binding mandates, APEC continues to serve as a vital platform for dialogue among nations with diverse political and economic systems. Participants stressed that maintaining open markets and regional integration remains crucial for mitigating supply chain disruptions and fostering shared long-term prosperity across the Asia-Pacific region.

stories.title: Pakistan Pace Bowlers Strike Early Against Sri Lanka in Second Test
stories.summary:
Pakistan's pace attack exploited a lively pitch to claim two vital wickets during the opening session of the third day in the second Test against Sri Lanka at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium. Resuming their second innings at 74-3, the visiting team advanced to 166-5 by lunch, leaving them trailing Pakistan by 60 runs as they fight to avoid an innings defeat. Fast bowler Aamer Jamal and teammate Razaullah spearheaded the morning breakthroughs.

Aamer provided the initial breakthrough in the first hour by trapping Dhananjaya de Silva lbw for 37 with a sharply incoming delivery that was upheld on review. Shortly after, Razaullah removed Pasindu Sooriyabandara for 38 off 116 balls, inducing a faint edge that wicket-keeper Ghazi Ghori caught through a diving effort. Sooriyabandara's patient knock provided crucial resistance on a surface marked by uneven bounce and considerable movement.

Pakistan managed the morning session without fast bowler Saqib Khan, who was ruled out of further bowling in the match due to a left hamstring strain sustained on Wednesday. Despite the absence, bowlers like Mohammad Abbas maintained pressure by repeatedly beating the bat, though he remained wicketless before the break. Sri Lankan captain Kusal Mendis and Sonal Dinusha successfully navigated the remainder of the session.

At the lunch interval, Kusal remained unbeaten on 32 alongside Dinusha, who was not out on 19. The pair stabilized the innings with an unbroken 40-run partnership for the sixth wicket. The match follows a drawn first Test at the same venue, leaving Pakistan in a commanding position as they seek a series victory.

stories.title: Pakistan Needs Five Wickets for Series Victory Against Sri Lanka
stories.summary:
Pakistan moved to the verge of a series-clinching victory in the second and final Test against Sri Lanka, needing just five more wickets on the third day in Rawalpindi. Sri Lanka reached 167-5 at the lunch break, still trailing Pakistan by 60 runs and fighting to avoid an innings defeat after posting a total of 325 in their first outing.

Resuming their second innings at 74-3, the visitors managed to add 93 runs during the morning session. However, Pakistan's pace attack dismantled the overnight partnership by removing both established batters. Aamer Jamal dismissed Dhananjaya de Silva for 37 via a sharp lbw decision, while Razaullah accounted for Pasindu Sooriyabandara, who scored 38 before being caught by a diving wicketkeeper Ghazi Ghori.

At the interval, Sri Lankan captain Kusal Mendis was holding firm with an unbeaten 32, accompanied by Sonal Dinusha, who was not out on 19. Jamal and Razaullah anchored the bowling effort with figures of 2-36 and 2-64 respectively. Pakistan's bowling depth was affected earlier by an injury to Saqib Khan, who pulled his hamstring and cannot bowl for the remainder of the fixture.

The ongoing contest follows the first Test of the series, which also concluded in a draw at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium. Pakistan now sits in a dominant position to secure the series win if they can quickly break the remaining resistance in the afternoon session.

stories.title: PPP Central Executive Committee to Review Bilawal Bhutto's Statement
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Peoples Party’s Central Executive Committee will formally discuss remarks made by Bilawal Bhutto regarding the approval of the proposed 27th Constitutional Amendment under duress. PPP spokesperson Nadeem Afzal Chan confirmed the upcoming deliberations during a television interview on Thursday, explaining the party's stance on constitutional reforms.

According to Chan, both the 26th and 27th constitutional amendments had originally been integrated into the party's manifesto on the condition that such legislative changes proved fruitful. When questioned about external pressure surrounding the 27th amendment, Chan declined to elaborate directly, instead pointing toward certain government elites. He also clarified that the implementation of Governor’s Rule did not require approval from the party's CEC, emphasizing that President Asif Ali Zardari operates free from pressure.

During the interview, Chan commented on internal political dynamics within the Pakistan Muslim League-Nawaz, specifically addressing the political standing of Talal Chaudhry. Chan claimed that Chaudhry now serves as the personal secretary to the interior minister and is no longer viewed as a core member by senior PML-N figures. He noted that Chaudhry, once closely aligned with Maryam Nawaz’s inner circle, is presently excluded from party meetings involving Nawaz Sharif or Maryam Nawaz.

In a separate development in Punjab, the provincial government launched a digital facility designed to simplify the division of family property. Through the Revenue Case Management System online portal, women can now utilize mobile phones to access the platform and assert their legal land ownership rights more easily.

stories.title: Sindh Chief Minister Proposes Wuhan-Style Urban Governance Pilot for Karachi
stories.summary:
Sindh Chief Minister Syed Murad Ali Shah has suggested launching a pilot project in a single district of Karachi based on the integrated city management system used in Wuhan, China. Speaking at a seminar in Karachi titled “Understanding China’s Governance & Deepening China-Pakistan Cooperation,” organized by the Karachi Council on Foreign Relations (KCFR), Mr. Shah highlighted China's strengths in long-term planning, interdepartmental coordination, and poverty reduction. The event was attended by Acting Chinese Consul General Dr. Feng Deheng, KCFR Chairperson Nadira Panjwani, along with various diplomats and government officials.

Drawing on insights from his recent visits to Hubei and Shanghai—particularly Wuhan’s City Operation and Management Centre—the chief minister noted how China's integrated framework connects different government departments on a common platform to monitor urban issues, identify risks, and handle public complaints. The proposed Karachi pilot would initially target everyday municipal problems such as waterlogging and flooded roads. It aims to establish clear responsibilities for registering complaints, coordinating departments, and ensuring prompt resolutions, backed by technical training and collaboration with Chinese municipal experts, local engineers, and academic institutions.

Mr. Shah also advocated for deeper municipal and academic ties between Karachi and Shanghai, which have been sister cities since 1984, including teacher-training programs and agricultural research partnerships. KCFR Chairperson Nadira Panjwani emphasized translating bilateral friendship into practical institutional cooperation, while Dr. Feng Deheng praised China's extensive poverty reduction achievements and reaffirmed China's commitment to supporting Pakistan's development path and the high-quality advancement of CPEC 2.0. The discussions mark the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations between Pakistan and China.

stories.title: Scores Feared Dead After Passenger Bus and Gas Bowser Collide in Gwadar
stories.summary:
A severe collision between a passenger bus and a gas bowser on the Makran Coastal Highway near Basool has left scores of people feared dead. According to ARY News, a massive fire immediately engulfed both vehicles following the impact. Eyewitnesses confirmed that women and children were among the passengers on board the bus.

Superintendent of Police Aslam Bangalzai stated that rescue teams were promptly dispatched to the accident location in Gwadar. Transporters reported that approximately 40 people, including women and children, were traveling on the passenger bus at the time of the crash. The ill-fated vehicle was journeying from Turbat to Karachi when the disaster occurred.

stories.title: Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir Briefed on Balochistan Counterterrorism Operations
stories.summary:
Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir received a detailed briefing on counterterrorism operations and security preparations during a visit to Turbat, Balochistan. According to the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), the army chief was updated on ongoing operations against externally sponsored terrorism and the progress of socioeconomic development initiatives in the region. Upon his arrival, he was received by the Corps Commander Balochistan and paid tribute by laying a floral wreath at the Shuhada Monument.

During his interactions with troops, Field Marshal Munir praised their high operational readiness and resolve to defend the country under challenging conditions. He reaffirmed the Pakistan Army's commitment to standing with the people of Balochistan in pursuing peace and sustainable development. This visit coincides with broader counterterrorism efforts across Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, where security forces recently killed numerous terrorists during intelligence-based operations, including 22 deaths recorded earlier in the week in South Waziristan, Bannu, and Tank.

The military's ongoing counterterrorism campaign operates under the vision of 'Azm-i-Istehkam' as approved by the Federal Apex Committee on National Action Plan. President Asif Ali Zardari commended the security forces for their bravery and professional conduct during these operations. Meanwhile, an independent monthly report by the Pakistan Institute for Conflict and Security Studies (PICSS) noted a significant nationwide decline in terrorism-related violence and militant attacks during October, with particularly pronounced improvements in Balochistan and mainland Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

stories.title: یوکرین جنگ کے بعد روسی ارب پتیوں کی پوتن کے سامنے خاموشی اور بے بسی
stories.summary: 24 فروری 2022 کو یوکرین پر حملے کے آغاز کے چند گھنٹے بعد روسی صدر ولادیمیر پوتن نے روس کے سب سے امیر افراد کو کریملن کے ایک ہال میں طلب کیا۔ اس اجلاس میں پوتن نے توقع ظاہر کی کہ یہ ارب پتی جنگ کی حمایت کریں گے اور معیشت کو سہارا دینے کے لیے حکومت کے ساتھ مل کر کام کریں گے۔ کریملن کی ویڈیو کے مطابق اس دوران کسی بھی کاروباری شخصیت نے ایک لفظ بھی نہیں بولا۔ پوتن کی حکومت کے دوران روسی اشرافیہ نے یہ سبق سیکھ لیا ہے کہ مخالفت کی کتنی بھاری قیمت چکانی پڑ سکتی ہے، جس کی واضح مثال 2003 میں میخائل خودورکوفسکی کی گرفتاری تھی جنہیں پوتن پر تنقید کرنے پر 10 سال جیل میں گزارناپڑے تھے۔ 2022 کے بعد سے کریملن نے جنگ کے ناقدین کے اثاثے ضبط کیے ہیں جبکہ وفاداروں کو منافع بخش سرکاری ٹھیکے دیے ہیں۔ اگرچہ فوربز کے مطابق روس میں ارب پتیوں کی تعداد اب بڑھ کر 155 ہو چکی ہے اور ان کی مجموعی دولت 700 ارب ڈالر تک پہنچ گئی ہے، لیکن مغربی پابندیوں اور بیرون ملک بائیکاٹ کے باعث یہ دولت انہیں سیاسی طاقت یا آزادی نہیں دیتی۔ اب پوتن کی عمر 74 برس ہو چکی ہے اور وہ ایک چوتھائی صدی سے اقتدار میں ہیں، جس کی وجہ سے روس کی اشرافیہ خاموشی سے اس بات پر غور کر رہی ہے کہ پوتن کے بعد کا منظرنامہ کیسا ہوگا۔ ماہرین اس کے بعد جمہوریت کے قیام کو مشکل قرار دیتے ہیں جبکہ نیا مطلق العناف رہنما یا 1990 کی دہائی کے اولیگاک نظام کی طرف واپسی کے امکانات پر غور کیا جا رہا ہے۔

stories.title: Trilateral Meeting in Shenzhen Sparks Global Focus Amid Complex Geopolitical Tensions
stories.summary:
The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China, has drawn intense global attention due to a planned three-way meeting between US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping, and Russian President Vladimir Putin. While a gathering among leaders of three major global powers offers an opportunity to address critical issues like nuclear non-proliferation, artificial intelligence regulation, and ongoing conflicts in Iran and Ukraine, practical outcomes are expected to face severe hurdles driven by differing geopolitical interests and underlying diplomatic strains.

Regarding nuclear non-proliferation, China’s expanding nuclear arsenal and its refusal to join arms control talks until reaching parity, alongside Russia's deepening military ties with North Korea, complicate prospects for genuine non-proliferation agreements. Similarly, cooperation on artificial intelligence is likely limited to basic safety warnings due to intense economic and military competition. On Middle Eastern and European conflicts, Russia and China derive strategic benefits from US involvement in the Middle East and finite resource allocation away from the Indo-Pacific, while continuing to support their respective positions despite high energy prices and ongoing warfare in Ukraine.

Furthermore, all three leaders arrive at the summit facing domestic political vulnerabilities: President Trump following Republican losses in US midterm elections, President Putin encountering battlefield challenges and drone attacks on Russian energy infrastructure, and President Xi dealing with domestic economic pressures and military leadership purges. A major concern remains whether an embattled Trump might attempt overly ambitious concessions reminiscent of the 1945 Yalta Conference, potentially ceding influence in Europe to Putin and in Asia to Xi. Analysts suggest that a simple diplomatic photo-op may ultimately be preferable to any risky or lopsided agreements.

stories.title: Australian Shares Extend Losses for Sixth Day Driven by Mining Slump
stories.summary:
Australian shares extended their downward trajectory for a sixth consecutive session, pushed lower primarily by slumping miners and gold stocks. Investors remained cautious as they assessed interest rate outlooks and awaited upcoming domestic employment figures. The S&P/ASX 200 index dropped 0.9% to reach 8,821.80 points by 2300 GMT.

Miners experienced a significant decline of 3.5%, hitting their weakest level since late March due to persistent weakness in copper prices, which fell to a seven-month low. Over recent sessions, this sub-index has lost approximately 14% despite a mild recovery in iron ore futures during the previous session. Individual mining giants suffered notable losses, with BHP shares falling 3.8% to an early-April low and Rio Tinto hovering near its weakest level since last December.

Gold stocks also retreated by 3.6% after hawkish signals from the US Federal Reserve pushed gold to a 14-month low, reinforcing expectations that interest rates will stay higher for longer. Consequently, shares of Northern Star Resources and Evolution Mining each declined by 3%. Meanwhile, the banking sector slipped 0.2%, putting that sub-index on track for its third consecutive session of losses, with National Australia Bank and Macquarie each dropping 0.6%.

Market participants closely monitored these developments ahead of Australia's October employment data release at 0030 GMT. The figures are expected to provide crucial insights into whether labour market conditions remain a concern for the Reserve Bank of Australia. Last month, RBA Governor Michele Bullock noted that the labour market remained tighter than previously assessed and that continued economic growth is necessary to bring sticky inflation back under control. In broader regional markets, New Zealand's S&P/NZX 50 index fell 0.2% to 14,264.29 points.

stories.title: Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir Visits Turbat to Review Security and Development
stories.summary:
Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir traveled to Turbat in Balochistan on Thursday to review the prevailing security environment, operational preparedness, and anti-terrorism efforts. According to a statement issued by the Inter-Services Public Relations, the visit emphasized the military's ongoing dedication to regional peace, prosperity, and sustainable development.

Upon his arrival in the region, the Chief of Defence Forces was welcomed by the Corps Commander Balochistan. Following his arrival, he paid his respects by laying a floral wreath at the Shuhada Monument and offering Fateha. The high-ranking official was then provided with a comprehensive briefing detailing ongoing operations targeting externally sponsored terrorism, alongside updates regarding various socio-economic development initiatives aimed at improving welfare for local residents.

During his time in the area, Field Marshal Munir interacted directly with military personnel stationed on the ground. He commended the troops for their high state of operational readiness, strong professionalism, and unwavering resolve to defend the country under challenging conditions.

Concluding his visit, Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir reiterated the Pakistan Army's firm commitment to standing alongside the people of Balochistan. He underscored that the military supports local efforts to achieve lasting peace, stability, and ongoing regional development.

stories.title: Japanese Equities Mixed as Investors Await Anthropic Listing and Metal Prices Drop
stories.summary:
Japanese equities experienced mixed trading on Thursday as investors maintained a cautious stance ahead of Anthropic's upcoming US stock market debut. At the same time, falling metal prices exerted downward pressure on non-ferrous metal stocks across the market. The Nikkei 225 Index managed a 0.71% increase to close at 59,444.21 following a session that swung between gains and losses, while the broader Topix edged down 0.04% to 3,822.47 in similarly choppy conditions.

In Tokyo, artificial intelligence and chip-related shares displayed varied performance. SoftBank Group shares rose by 4.5%, whereas Advantest lost 0.55%. Anthropic secured $81.3 billion in what marks the largest stock-market debut on record by upsizing its offering and pricing shares at $83 apiece—above its initial range of $70 to $78—valuing the Claude chatbot maker at $1.5 trillion ahead of its Nasdaq trading debut. Market commentators noted that cash-raising sales of existing tech stocks ahead of the listing may have driven recent market corrections.

Market breadth remained negative throughout the session, recording 127 decliners against 95 advancers and 3 unchanged issues. Japan's non-ferrous metal index dropped 2.8% to an 11-month low as gold prices slid to a 14-month low and copper touched a seven-month trough. JX Advanced Metals led the losses on the Nikkei by falling 6.2% to its lowest level since last December, alongside declines of 5.24% for Sumitomo Metal Mining and 4.6% for Mitsubishi Materials.

Conversely, certain equities posted notable gains on the day. Trend Micro emerged as the top gainer on the Nikkei index with a 5.72% increase, followed closely by Taiyo Yuden, which rose by 4.6%. Analysts suggested that broader market sentiment could potentially improve once the Anthropic listing is completed and the associated selling pressure runs its course.

stories.title: Thai Baht Holds Steady Against the US Dollar on Thursday
stories.summary:
The Thai baht remained largely unchanged against the US dollar during Thursday's trading session. Financial data from LSEG indicated that the local currency held steady near previous levels as the trading day progressed.

At 0221 GMT, the baht registered a marginal increase of 0.04%, trading at 33.96 against the US dollar. Throughout the early part of the session, the currency moved within a narrow trading range between 33.940 and 34.005.

This performance follows the previous session, during which the Thai baht finished at a rate of 33.975 per US dollar. Market activity for the currency remained subdued with limited movement relative to the dollar.

stories.title: London Copper Recovers Modestly Following Steep Losses Led by Strong Dollar
stories.summary:
London copper prices experienced a modest recovery on Thursday, rising slightly after tumbling to their lowest point in seven months during the previous session.
